name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Joaquin Castro running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger minimally funded with no outside support
Prediction markets price Castro near certain to win
model.rationale: Castro holds a D+16 district, is a well-known incumbent, and has out-raised his opponent more than tenfold, while Polymarket prices his win at 97%. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting otherwise, this stays firmly Safe D.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or Castro retirement would be the main way this race could tighten, though nothing in the evidence points that way.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in a San Antonio-area district that leans Democratic by sixteen points. He is a well-established incumbent who has raised over half a million dollars, while Republican Edgardo Baez has raised under fifty thousand and has no outside spending behind him. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets put Castro's chances at about 97 percent.

The fundamentals strongly favor the incumbent: the district's partisan lean, Castro's incumbency advantage, and his financial edge all point the same direction. The race is rated Safe D, with the only real uncertainty being turnout variation in a low-profile contest.
